issues.legal_issue: Interest in a mortgage suit is governed by the mortgage-specific procedural provision rather than the general provision for interest in money decrees.
material_facts: The bank brought a suit to recover a loan on the basis of a mortgage.
The trial court awarded interest after the filing of the suit at a rate below the contractual rate.
The High Court relied on the general provision for interest in money decrees when it substituted the contractual rate.
issues.conclusion: The mortgage-specific provision applies to interest in a mortgage suit; the general provision governing interest in money decrees does not apply.
issues.legal_principle: Order 34 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure governs interest in suits for foreclosure, sale, and redemption of mortgages, while Section 34 governs simple money decrees. The Court relied on its decisions in Jaigobind Singh v. Lachmi Narain Ram and Soli Pestonji Majoo v. Gangadhar Khemka, and on State Bank of Mysore v. G.P. Thulasi Bai.

predicates.mortgage_recovery_proceeding: A creditor brought a proceeding to recover a debt on the basis of a mortgage.
predicates.interest_after_filing_is_at_issue: The court had to determine interest accruing after the proceeding was filed.

issues.definition: When a creditor seeks recovery on a mortgage and post-filing interest is at issue, the mortgage-specific interest framework applies.

issues.legal_issue: A court deciding interest in a mortgage suit may award post-filing interest below the contractual rate when it exercises its discretion under the mortgage-specific rule.
material_facts: The loan was secured by an equitable mortgage.

The trial court considered the interest issue, expressly exercised its discretion, and awarded simple interest at six per cent after the suit was filed rather than the contractual rate of 16.5 per cent.
The High Court replaced that rate with the contractual rate.
issues.conclusion: The court had discretion to award post-filing interest below the contractual rate, and it was not bound to award the contractual rate in all circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: Order 34 Rule 11 CPC uses the word “may,” which confers discretion over interest for the periods addressed by clauses (a) and (b). After the 1929 amendment, awarding the contractual rate after suit is not obligatory even where the rate is not penal, excessive, or substantially unfair under the Usurious Loans Act, 1918. The Court relied on Jaigobind Singh v. Lachmi Narain Ram, Soli Pestonji Majoo v. Gangadhar Khemka, Srinivasa Vardachariar v. Gopala Menon, and K. Manickchand v. Elias Saleh Mohamed Sait.

predicates.mortgage_recovery_proceeding: A creditor brought a proceeding to recover a debt on the basis of a mortgage.
predicates.court_is_fixing_post_filing_interest: The court is determining the rate of interest for a period after the proceeding was filed.

issues.definition: In a mortgage recovery proceeding, when the court fixes post-filing interest, it may set a rate below the contractual rate.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory restriction on reopening bank transactions for excessive interest does not displace the court’s discretion to set post-filing interest in a mortgage suit.
material_facts: The creditor was a bank and the loan was secured by a mortgage.
The bank argued that the statutory protection for bank interest rates prevented the court from reducing the contractual rate during the suit.
The disputed rate was post-filing interest, and the trial court had exercised its discretion under the mortgage-specific procedural rule.
issues.conclusion: Section 21-A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 does not override Order 34 Rule 11 CPC or remove the court’s discretion over post-filing interest in a mortgage suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21-A’s non-obstante clause applies to the Usurious Loans Act, 1918 and other state laws relating to indebtedness; it does not override the Code of Civil Procedure. The discretion under Order 34 Rule 11 is independent of the Usurious Loans Act. The Court applied Aswini Kumar Ghosh v. Arabinda Bose on construing a non-obstante clause and distinguished Corporation Bank v. D.S. Gowda and Bank of Baroda v. Rednam Nagachaya Devi, which did not decide whether Section 21-A displaced the discretion at issue.

predicates.banking_transaction: A bank entered into a lending transaction with a debtor.
predicates.mortgage_recovery_proceeding: A creditor brought a proceeding to recover a debt on the basis of a mortgage.
predicates.post_filing_interest_is_at_issue: The court had to determine interest accruing after the proceeding was filed.

issues.definition: When a bank transaction is the subject of a mortgage recovery proceeding and post-filing interest is at issue, the bank-interest protection does not displace the court’s discretion over that interest.

issues.legal_issue: A higher court errs by replacing a trial court’s discretionary post-filing interest award in a mortgage suit solely on the basis that the contractual rate is mandatory under the general rule for money decrees.
material_facts: The trial court expressly exercised its discretion and awarded six per cent simple interest after the suit was filed.
The High Court substituted the contractual rate, relying on Section 34 CPC and not applying Order 34 Rule 11 CPC.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s order was set aside and the trial court’s post-filing interest rate was restored.
issues.legal_principle: In a mortgage suit, Order 34 Rule 11 CPC, not Section 34 CPC, governs post-filing interest and allows the court to depart from the contractual rate. The Court relied on Jaigobind Singh v. Lachmi Narain Ram, Soli Pestonji Majoo v. Gangadhar Khemka, and State Bank of Mysore v. G.P. Thulasi Bai.

predicates.appeal_from_modified_mortgage_decree: A party brought an appeal from a higher court’s modification of an interest award in a mortgage decree.
predicates.trial_court_exercised_post_filing_intere: The trial court expressly exercised discretion in setting the interest rate for the period after the suit was filed.
predicates.higher_court_replaced_rate_as_contractua: The higher court substituted the contractual rate on the ground that it was mandatory.

issues.definition: On an appeal from a modified mortgage decree, if the trial court exercised discretion over post-filing interest and the higher court replaced the rate as mandatory, the trial court’s award is restored.
